title: Volume 1 Chapter 3: To You Who Are Surprisingly Close, and to You Who Feel Breathtakingly Far Away 5
content: “Are you kidding me? Are you kidding me? Longdagger-sama!”
Rana, a staff member of the Adventurer Guild, confirmed it twice. Her face was desperate, almost pleading.
“What do you mean kidding? It’s right in front of you.”

I pointed with my gaze at the enormous magic stone of the Forest Dragon, which was more like occupying the table than simply sitting on it. It was larger than a single embrace. Carrying it back to the city was a hassle since I couldn’t wrap my arms around it.

However, Rana refused to look at the gigantic stone, desperately turning her face away as if it wouldn’t enter her line of sight no matter what. It was less a futile resistance and more of a meaningless one.
“I enjoyed hearing the amusing joke about defeating the Master of the Grassland, so please tell me the truth. What kind of magic stone is this?”
“It’s from the Forest Dragon, a designated target for subjugation in the Grassland.”
“I’m not looking for any rhetorical devices!”
Rana shouted, a noisy woman indeed. I wished she would take a little cue from Erika’s always calm demeanor; even one-tenth of it would be something.
I had come back to the city quickly after achieving today’s goal, but Rana’s ruckus was quite the distraction.
It was just past noon, so the Adventurer Guild was empty, but there were still adventurers and guild staff around. With all this noise, it was bound to attract attention.
As I glanced around, for some reason, no one was looking our way. It felt as if they were intentionally averting their eyes.
What’s going on here?
“Is this really the magic stone from the Grassland’s thing?”
Rana asked tiredly, furrowing her brow as if she were enduring a headache.
Her expression seemed to suggest that if she said the name, it would somehow confirm the truth.
When I silently nodded, Rana let out a short groan.
“There was actually another one, but I think it’s buried underground somewhere.”
Guaah! At my words, Rana clutched her head and howled.
“Fine, fine then.”
The way Rana muttered while looking down was a bit frightening.
“It will take some time to confirm the subjugation of the designated target, but we can buy the magic stone right away. What would you like to do?”
For some reason, Rana suddenly asked with a flat expression. I wondered if there was some rule that all women around me, except for Erika, had to be emotionally stable.
“Then I’ll leave it to you.”
“Understood. Once the subjugation confirmation is complete, I will pay you the subjugation reward separately, so I will inform you once it’s confirmed.”
“Ah, by the way, did I do something bad?”
“Not at all. I’m just going to be busy arranging adventurers for the confirmation and the subjugation reward, which means I’ll definitely be working overtime.”
Ahahaha, Rana laughed.
“Somehow, whenever Longdagger-san enters the Adventurer Guild, I suddenly get sent to the counter. Why is that? I mean, there are other counters, so why do you come to mine, Longdagger-san?”
It seemed that all the various tasks for the adventurers fell to that guild staff member.
“Sorry about that…”
I had chosen Rana’s counter because I recognized her, but it seemed to have been quite the hassle.

“No, no, it’s fine! A part of the handling fee goes into my pocket. It’s just that with such a gigantic magic stone, it’s going to auction, so the effort doesn’t quite match up. But really, it’s fine! I have no trouble with money!”
She said, laughing heartily.
“I had just finished dealing with the magic stones from the Golden Ogre!”

For some reason, while looking up at me with a cheerful face, Rana proceeded with the purchase procedures for the magic stone. As I was leaving, she cheerfully said, “I’ll be working overtime from now on! Also, the auction’s share is on deferred payment!”
I truly felt bad about it.
The magic stone from the Forest Dragon was worth more than three magic stones from the Golden Ogre.

Even if split in half, it was still more than the previous reward. Moreover, I would also receive a portion of the money from the auction and the subjugation reward. It was more than enough as a down payment for a house.

Shara, who received half of it, screamed. “I don’t want it! I don’t need it! The church doesn’t operate for money!” she wailed, but when I told her, “If you don’t take it now, the subjugation reward and auction share will increase,” she ran off to the orphanage, crying while clutching the bag of gold.
The meals at the orphanage would be lavish for a while.
Children, eat meat! Meat two, vegetables one!

After parting with Shara, we decided to head to the merchant who was waiting for the house payment, now that we had the money. Since Erika had been exiled from Faltarl, we had kept him waiting for quite a while. It wasn’t our fault, but if we could pay, we wanted to do it quickly.

When we arrived at the store we had heard about, the merchant greeted us with suspicion. After all, from his perspective, it was just yesterday that he had asked us to pay. What business could we possibly have showing up the next day? He might have expected us to ask him to wait.
So when we handed over the money, the merchant was greatly surprised. The expression on his face was more like, “Why didn’t you pay yesterday when you had the money?”
I explained that I had defeated the Forest Dragon today, and that there was still additional reward money coming, showing him the promissory note issued by the guild.
The merchant’s face, as he looked at me with an indescribable expression upon seeing the note, was quite memorable.
He looked like he suspected a scam. I felt like saying I understood his feelings, but I held back.

Erika, who had accomplished the nonsensical feat of earning that amount in just one day, wore a face that said it was only natural. If that was the case, then I had to wear a face that said, “What’s wrong with that?” I didn’t feel like I had pulled it off well.
“Uh, I look forward to working with you in the future?”
I felt a strange sympathy for the merchant as he replied, confused.
Thus, Erika and I completed our first job as proper adventurers, not just haphazardly, but by choosing and fulfilling quests for our own purposes.
Whether it was proper to subjugate the guild’s designated target was another matter entirely.
The unfamiliar sound of birds chirping. The moment Erika woke up, she thought about such things.
Even such things made her realize that she was not at her family home. Erika chuckled at her unexpectedly delicate self while combing her disheveled hair with her fingers and slowly getting dressed.

If there was anything good about leaving her family home, it was this. She didn’t have to put on a noble face in front of the servants from the morning. Stretching her body lightly, Erika let out a small yawn.
After washing her face and heading to the living room, she found her nominal husband baking bread.
Incredibly, he had a piece of bread in his mouth while doing so.
How strange. Unlike her, who had lost her noble status, Shin was still a proper noble.
“Good morning! Want some bread?”
What kind of world has a noble son baking bread with a piece of bread in his mouth? Well, he was right in front of her, and Erika was bewildered.
But within moments, she tossed her confusion aside and returned the morning greeting, preparing tea. If she let herself be confused by this much with Shin, the day would end before she knew it.
She couldn’t cook, but she could at least brew tea. Erika filled the pot with water and lit the stove, which she had only recently learned to use.
Next to her, as Shin added another piece of bread while flipping it over with a pathetic “Uwa-chicchi,” it was slightly burnt.
“That one’s mine.”
Shin muttered quietly, and she felt a little happy.
She took the toasted bread and boiling water to the table, skipping many formalities as she poured the tea into cups.
Shin hastily offered thanks to the gods, while Erika took her time to do so more politely. There was no particular conversation, but strangely, it felt calming.

It was a strange thing. Until recently, they had been classmates, yet she had never spoken to him properly, and now she didn’t mind the silence between them. Even though she had lived in a world where silence was golden and silence was a weapon, this boy scattered a silence that was neither.
The best thing about leaving her family home was—, as she thought that far, Erika became aware.
She was now—what a thing it was—.
To think that she was grateful for being “exiled.”
Without meaning to, Erika burst into laughter.
What a ridiculous story.
What a terrible story.
Not a lie to comfort herself. To say that being exiled allowed her to avoid putting on a noble face from the morning. And in the end, was she grateful for being exiled because she could meet Shin?
How absurdly ridiculous it was, the ones who exiled her would surely be dumbfounded.
Erika was astonished by her unstoppable smile.
Indeed, if that were the case, she would cling to living in this house. She would cling to living with Shin in this house. This was truly a symbol for her.
The freedom she had long since thrown away, the freedom to choose for herself.
That symbol was this house, and also Shin.
Noticing that she had suddenly started chuckling, Erika realized Shin was looking at her with a strange expression. For a moment, he looked anxious.
“Uh, was my way of eating bread strange?”
Hiyu! She suppressed the laughter that was about to escape with all her might.
As a lady, it wouldn’t do to burst out laughing.
“No, Shin, that’s not it, not at all, Shin.”
Even so, she gently wiped away the tears that had formed at the corners of her eyes.
For some reason, it was impossible not to find Shin’s concern about his way of eating amusing.
A person who had thrown away their life to gain a best friend and acquaintance, standing beside her with nothing but a sword, was worried about how to eat bread. It made no sense.
“Yes, I’m just a little grateful to be having breakfast with you like this.”
She found herself saying something that made no sense. What did gratitude mean? Was she smiling out of gratitude?
Hmm, Shin took a sip of tea and wore a serious expression.
What would he say this time? Erika became aware of her strange expectations.
“Then I should smile too.”
Shin smiled.
“I’m grateful to be able to have breakfast with you.”
Considering Shin’s position, that was probably a forced smile.
Erika thought so, but she was strangely drawn to that smile, and a smile escaped her as well. She felt inexplicably happy.
To my best friend,

Erika began writing a letter to the Light Priestess in Faltarl. After breakfast, Shin mentioned he wanted to do a bit of sewing, which left her with some free time. She had actually wanted to work as an adventurer again today, but now she was free. There was plenty of time.
As she wrote, she thought that she probably wouldn’t send this letter.
Even if she did, she didn’t think it would reach anyone.
So, this was more like a diary disguised as a letter.

Writing a letter with no intention of sending it felt somewhat like clinging to the past, but despite that doubt, her words flowed without any such sentiment. While she expressed concern for her best friend’s health and recent happenings, her own feelings were written down honestly, like a diary, and they were all bright and cheerful.
Whose influence could it be?
As she pondered this, she realized she had been writing a lot about Shin.
No, that’s not right. If she wrote about her life since being exiled, he would inevitably be there.
If she wrote that being an adventurer was surprisingly fun, Shin would be part of that.
If she wrote about her first meal at an adventurer's diner, he would also be there.
It was only natural, Erika thought with a wry smile.
Since they met in that carriage, he had always been by her side.
Even though she was someone who could make men nervous, it was even stranger to have such a laid-back boy nearby. A smile escaped her as she continued writing.
What kind of face would the boy, who shared a vibe similar to her best friend the Light Priestess, make when he finally met her? She paused for a moment, her pen hovering.
She stopped writing, momentarily caught up in an unknown emotion, but no answer came.
What was it? After a few moments of pondering with no conclusion, she resumed writing.
Well, when that time comes, she would introduce him. "I am her best friend. If I introduce him, her impression of him will surely change. Let’s make it happen."
Erika tossed aside the lingering, vague feelings and finished the letter.
She had felt hungry from the aroma wafting in from the living room.
Perhaps it would be good to learn how to cook herself.
And she still wanted to work as an adventurer today; living the adventurer's life with Shin was undeniably enjoyable.
Thinking about such things, Erika opened the door.
Ah, so this is the life of an exiled marquis daughter as an adventurer; it sounds like a cheap play from the royal capital. But for now, she was playing the role of a couple in this farce.
They suited each other, and it seemed quite fun.
“Shin!”
The voice calling the name of the boy she shared this life with was filled with more expectation than she had anticipated.
What would this adventurer's life bring her from now on?
Erika Solnzali declared.
Her voice was truly noble, arrogant, and filled with joy.
“Today, we’re living the adventurer's life again!”
